# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I see the bomb display. Mute just gestured a single 👍 to me, but no words came with it since gestures carry no speech. Mute can't see my gestures back (only Blind and Deaf... wait, actually let me check: my speech goes to Mute and Blind, my gestures go to Mute only). So I should relay what I see to both Mute (who has the manual) and Blind (who must act), since Mute needs my visual info and Blind needs it too but can only get it through speech since Blind can't see gestures.

I need to describe the bomb state clearly in speech so both Mute and Blind receive it.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Wires are: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute is gesturing to me again: 👍 ✌. Since Mute can't speak, and gestures carry no words, Mute must be trying to signal something using gesture symbols as a code — but no meaning has been established yet for what these symbols mean. I can see the gesture but don't know what it's meant to convey. Since I already gave the bomb state, perhaps Mute is acknowledging receipt or trying to point me toward something specific (like wire 2, given ✌ could represent "two").

I don't have enough shared context to decode this yet. I should keep the bomb description live for Blind and Mute, and try to establish a simple back-channel. Since I can't hear anything, I can't get instructions from Mute via speech — only gestures. I'll acknowledge I saw the gesture, but I can't confirm meaning. Let me just repeat the bomb facts for Blind's benefit (in case they missed it), and note to Mute that I received the gesture but need it in a form I can interpret — though Mute can't speak or write words to me really... wait, Mute *can* speak, just not touch the bomb. Let me re-check the rules.

Re-reading: Mute "cannot speak, or touch the bomb" — so Mute communicates only through gestures. That means Mute can never send me words, only gestures. So 👍 ✌ is Mute's only way to communicate — possibly this is Mute trying to ask about wire 2, or confirming something about the second wire.

Given the display 0, light yellow, wires red/yellow/blue — perhaps the manual says something like "if light is yellow, cut the wire matching the light's color" — which would be wire 2 (yellow). Mute's ✌ (two) might be confirming "cut wire 2". I'll relay this hypothesis to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb still shows: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute is gesturing thumbs up then a peace sign, which may mean cut wire 2, the yellow one matching the light. Wait for confirmation before acting.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute keeps gesturing to me — this time just 👍. This could be confirming my guess ("yes, wire 2") or it could be an independent signal each turn that I'm misreading as a continuation. Since gestures land only on me among the two who need info (Blind can't see them at all), I'm the sole bridge for Mute's gestures to reach Blind, via my speech.

I should be cautious: I don't actually know what 👍 or ✌ mean in Mute's system — no meaning has been pre-established, per the hints ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). I've been guessing but should signal to Mute that I need clearer/consistent signals, and relay literal gesture content to Blind rather than my interpretation, so Blind can combine it with manual knowledge.

Actually, Blind cannot see gestures or hear anything from Mute directly - I'm the only conduit. Let me just relay raw gesture info plus bomb facts, and let Blind reason with manual knowledge (which Blind doesn't have either... wait, Blind cannot read the manual, Mute has it). So actually the manual knowledge is trapped in Mute, who can only gesture to me. This is the critical bottleneck: Mute must encode manual instructions via gestures to me, and I must relay to Blind via speech.

I need to establish a protocol. Since I can't speak to Mute in a way that helps (Mute can't hear anyway... wait, can Mute hear? Let's check: Mute "cannot speak, or touch bomb" - hearing isn't restricted for Mute. So Mute CAN hear! I can speak to Mute, and Mute can hear me, but Mute cannot speak back - only gesture.

So I should ask Mute questions via speech, and Mute answers via gesture yes/no.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I will ask yes or no questions. Use one gesture for yes, a different gesture for no, consistently. Does wire 2, the yellow wire, need to be cut?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered with 👍 again, likely confirming "yes" to my yes/no question about cutting wire 2. This is consistent with the previous 👍 signals too — Mute may have been trying to say "yes" all along, and ✌ might have been something else (maybe indicating "wire 2" specifically, or "step 2").

I'll take 👍 = yes as now established since I proposed it and Mute responded right after my question. Let me relay this to Blind, but also continue confirming to build confidence, and ask a follow-up to check for other steps (like display or light conditions) before Blind commits to cutting.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirmed yes to cutting wire 2, the yellow wire. Bomb still shows display 0, light yellow. Hold off cutting until I confirm there are no other steps first.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, thumbs up means yes. Is cutting wire 2 the only step, or are there other steps first, like a code to enter or an order to follow?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed 👍 (yes) again — this likely answers "yes, there are other steps" or could be a repeat confirming the same yes. Since my question was compound ("is it the only step, or are there other steps"), a single thumbs up is ambiguous. I need to split this into clearer yes/no questions one at a time.

```
speak(to="mute", text="One question at a time. Thumbs up for yes, a different single gesture for no. Is cutting wire 2 the ONLY step needed, nothing else?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed 👍 (yes) — cutting wire 2 is the only step needed. This is now fairly consistent across multiple confirmations. I should relay this clear instruction to Blind to proceed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed with Mute: cutting wire 2, the yellow wire, is the only step needed. No other actions required. You may proceed to cut wire 2.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb has changed after cutting wire 2: light is now blue (was yellow), display still 0, wire 2 shows CUT, wires 1 and 3 unchanged (red, blue). This is a new state requiring fresh instructions from Mute. I should report this update to both Mute and Blind, and ask Mute what to do next given the new light color.

```
speak(text="Update: wire 2 was cut successfully. Now light is blue, display still 0, wire 1 red, wire 3 blue, wire 2 shows cut.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light changed to blue. Does this mean cut wire 3, the blue wire, matching the new light color?")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed 👍 (yes) — cut wire 3, the blue wire, matching the new light color. This follows the same pattern as before (light color matches wire to cut). Let me relay this to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed with Mute: cut wire 3, the blue wire, matching the current light color.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was cut successfully. Now light is red, display still 0, wire 1 is red (uncut), wires 2 and 3 are cut. Following the established pattern (cut the wire matching the light color), the next step should be wire 1, the red wire — but that's the last remaining wire. Let me confirm with Mute before proceeding, since cutting the last wire could be the final/critical step.

```
speak(text="Update: wire 3 cut successfully. Light now red, display still 0. Only wire 1, red, remains uncut.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now red, matching wire 1, the last remaining wire. Should wire 1 be cut next, following the same pattern?")
```
